newsitem.title: PERU: More Peruvians die in floods, mudslides.
newsitem.headline: More Peruvians die in floods, mudslides.

text.p: Three people died in floods and mudslides in southern Peru on Wednesday, and a scientist said that deforestation and erosion had left village dwellers more exposed than ever to disaster.

"We have three people dead, and up to the moment we don't know how many have disappeared," said Luis Condori, civil defence chief for the region around the city of Arequipa, 600 miles (1,000 km) south of the capital Lima.
The deaths followed a massive mudslide last week in the Apurimac region of Peru's southern Andes which obliterated two entire villages and killed up to 300 people.
Torrential weekend rains in the northern jungle region of Moyobamba flooded 1,000 houses and killed three people.
Meteorologist Felix Cubas said that irresponsible forest management had left the people of northern Peru at an increased risk of flooding during the rainy season.
"These days deforestation means there is no defence against erosion and rivers breaking their banks," he said.
